:::{#thm-half-space-dimension}
#### Differences of points in a hyperplane and in a half-space

Let $\vec{w} \in \reals^p$ be nonzero, let $b \in \reals$,
and let $\mathcal{H}$, $\mathcal{H}^+$ be the hyperplane and open half-space of @def-half-space.
For a set $S \subseteq \reals^p$, let $D(S) \eqdef \cb{\vy - \vx : \vx, \vy \in S}$
be the set of differences of its points.

1. $D(\mathcal{H}) = \cb{\vecf{s} : \dprod{\vec{w}}{\vecf{s}} = 0}$,
   a subspace of dimension $p - 1$.
2. $D(\mathcal{H}^+) = \reals^p$, a subspace of dimension $p$.

The same holds for $\mathcal{H}^-$.

:::

::: proof

**Part 1.**
Let $\vx, \vy \in \mathcal{H}$.
By @thm-hyperplane-subspace part 3, $\vec{w} \cdot (\vy - \vx) = 0$,
so $\vy - \vx \in \mathcal{H}_0 = \cb{\vecf{s} : \dprod{\vec{w}}{\vecf{s}} = 0}$.
Conversely, fix any $\vx_0 \in \mathcal{H}$ (it exists by @thm-hyperplane-subspace part 2).
For any $\vecf{s} \in \mathcal{H}_0$, the point $\vx_0 + \vecf{s}$ is in $\mathcal{H}$ by the same part,
and $(\vx_0 + \vecf{s}) - \vx_0 = \vecf{s}$.
So $D(\mathcal{H}) = \mathcal{H}_0$, which has dimension $p - 1$ by @thm-hyperplane-subspace part 1.

**Part 2.**
Every difference is in $\reals^p$, so $D(\mathcal{H}^+) \subseteq \reals^p$.
For the other direction, fix any $\vx_0 \in \mathcal{H}$ and any $\vecf{v} \in \reals^p$.
For a number $t > 0$ to be chosen, let $\vx_t \eqdef \vx_0 + t\,\vec{w}$.
Then

$$
\ba
\dprod{\vec{w}}{\vx_t} + b
&= \paren{\dprod{\vec{w}}{\vx_0} + b} + t\,\dprod{\vec{w}}{\vec{w}}
&& \text{(linearity of } \vx \mapsto \dprod{\vec{w}}{\vx} \text{)}
\\
&= t\,\dprod{\vec{w}}{\vec{w}},
&& \text{(} \vx_0 \in \mathcal{H} \text{)}
\ea
$$

which is positive, so $\vx_t \in \mathcal{H}^+$.
Next,

$$
\ba
\vec{w}\' (\vx_t + \vecf{v}) + b
&= \paren{\dprod{\vec{w}}{\vx_t} + b} + \dprod{\vec{w}}{\vecf{v}}
&& \text{(linearity of } \vx \mapsto \dprod{\vec{w}}{\vx} \text{)}
\\
&= t\,\dprod{\vec{w}}{\vec{w}} + \dprod{\vec{w}}{\vecf{v}}.
&& \text{(the display above)}
\ea
$$

Because $\dprod{\vec{w}}{\vec{w}} > 0$, this is positive once $t > -\dprod{\vec{w}}{\vecf{v}} / \dprod{\vec{w}}{\vec{w}}$.
Choose such a $t > 0$.
Then $\vx_t$ and $\vx_t + \vecf{v}$ are both in $\mathcal{H}^+$,
and their difference is $\vecf{v}$.
So $\vecf{v} \in D(\mathcal{H}^+)$.
The whole space $\reals^p$ is a subspace of dimension $p$ (@def-dimension).

The proof for $\mathcal{H}^-$ is the same with $-\vec{w}$ and $-b$ in place of $\vec{w}$ and $b$.
:::
